CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Implement the already-announced matching 25% tariffs on ~$34B of U.S. goods (soybeans, autos, seafood, dairy) on 6 July, in lockstep with the U.S. List 1 action. Do not expand beyond that matching list now, and do not reopen unilateral purchase commitments after Washington discarded the May joint statement. Keep a channel for talks, but treat credibility of proportionate response as the binding constraint on the eve of first implementation.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not yet existential. USTR’s 15 June final plan puts 25% on List 1 (~$34B, 818 lines, effective 6 July) aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics and machinery—i.e., Made in China 2025 sectors—with List 2 (~$16B) still coming (timeline 2018-06-15; USTR 15 June release). Trump on 18 June directed identification of an additional ~$200B at 10% if China answers the $50B action, and public commentary notes a further $200B threat that China cannot match dollar-for-dollar (timeline 2018-06-18; Lexology 27 June). The April ZTE denial order showed the U.S. can halt a national champion overnight; the June fine-and-compliance deal and 2 July limited operating authorization ease that shock, but Senate 85–10 language to reinstate penalties means the firm-level lever is not retired (timeline 2018-04-16; Politico 3 July). FX is already transmitting stress: CNY weakened from ~6.32 in February to 6.6368 on 3 July (DEXCHUS) and 6.7164 on the July monthly print (EXCHUS, +6.3% in the window); CNBC (3 July) had onshore/offshore through 6.7, the weakest in ~11 months, with June losses of ~3.25%. That sits near the +0.5 CHN anchor (FX pressure, tech targeting) but short of it: industrial production is still ~6% YoY (CHNPRINTO 106.0), reserves are ~$3.14T and only ~0.5% lower, and U.S. goods imports from China actually jumped (IMPCH 38.96B in February to 47.01B in July) as buyers front-ran duties. The May 19 joint statement (China to “significantly increase” purchases; Mnuchin “on hold”) collapsed on 29 May when the White House proceeded anyway (timeline 2018-05-19, 2018-05-29), so further unsecured purchase concessions would be pocketed. Matching retaliation is therefore the least-bad action: MOFCOM already said it would hit the same scale and intensity and that prior talk outcomes are void; Lu Kang said China “has no choice but to fight back forcefully” while not wanting a trade war (NPR 15 June; Diplomat 16 June). Going beyond the $34B list now would more quickly invite the $200B process; blinking after announcing would invite more U.S. pressure. Hold the second $16B to the U.S. timetable and leave room to negotiate once Washington shows it will not unilaterally reopen lists.
key_factors: July 6 U.S. List 1 ($34B/25%) and China matching list take effect tomorrow
Live U.S. threat of ~$200B more if China retaliates; China cannot match further rounds 1:1
CNY already down sharply (through ~6.64–6.72) on trade-war risk; IP and reserves still stable
May 19 purchase truce collapsed 10 days later — unsecured concessions failed
ZTE denial order demonstrated entity-list risk; rescue deal is incomplete and Congress is hostile

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR announces final two-stage $50B tariff plan: 25% on List 1 (~$34B, 818 lines, effective July 6) and List 2 (~$16B, later). China announces matching retaliation the same day.
Trump directs USTR to identify an additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates against the $50B action.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
CNY/USD 6.6368 on 2018-07-03 vs ~6.32 in Feb; +2.15% in the reported window, with a sharp break after mid-June.
China industrial production still 106.0 (same period previous year = 100) as of 2018-07-01; growth intact, not a hard landing.
U.S. goods imports from China 47.01B in July print vs 38.96B in February — front-loading, not yet a realized export collapse.
Lu Kang: China doesn't want a trade war but "has no choice but to fight back forcefully" to safeguard national interests and the multilateral system.
China published two lists to match the U.S. plan (July 6 + later). Trump directed identification of $200B at 10%; a further $200B was threatened. China cannot respond in kind to ~$450B.
Yuan weakest in ~11 months; onshore/offshore through 6.7; June fall of 3.25% compared to 2015, described as market-driven trade-war risk.
Commerce authorized limited ZTE operations 2 July–August while seeking to lift the April ban; Senate voted 85-10 to reinstate tough penalties.
